title: He covers you again, and again, and again
subtitle: The One who forgives and conceals sins as often as you return
intro: Al-Ghaffar (الْغَفَّارُ) means the Ever-Forgiving, the One who covers the sins of His servants over and over, however many times they fall and come back. It speaks to the person who keeps slipping on the same thing and fears that this time the door will be shut.

root.sense: Ghafr means to cover and conceal. The Arabs called the helmet a mighfar because it covers the head and shields it from blows. Maghfira is His covering of a sin: it is hidden from others and you are protected from its harm. The form Ghaffar stresses repetition, covering again and again.

row.title: I have asked too many times
sub: Surely His patience has run out

row.title: Return, and He covers again
sub: His forgiving does not wear out

knowing: Al-Ghaffar is the forgiveness of repetition. Where human patience runs thin after the third apology, His covering returns each time the servant sincerely returns. {idea}The name is shaped for frequency: not forgiveness once, but forgiveness as a habit of His.{/idea}

Its root is covering. When Allah forgives as Al-Ghaffar, He lays a cover over the sin, as you cover a dish to keep it from view, or as a helmet covers the head from harm. You are shielded from its punishment, and He does not expose you before others. The sin may still be written in your record, but it is covered and no longer counts against you.

Three times in the Quran this name is joined to Al-Aziz, the Almighty (38:66, 39:5, 40:42). {idea}His forgiving is not the forgiving of someone who cannot punish.{/idea} He has full power over the sinner and chooses, again and again, to cover instead. That is the difference between His forgiveness and ours: ours is often helplessness, His is pure generosity.
seeing: Nuh spent centuries calling a stubborn people. Still his message was: seek your Lord's forgiveness, for He is Ghaffar, and He will send rain, wealth, children, gardens and rivers (71:10-12). The door he held open was a door of repeated forgiveness for people who had refused him for generations.

The Prophet ﷺ described a servant who sins and says, My Lord, forgive me, and Allah says, My servant knew he has a Lord who forgives sins and holds to account; I have forgiven him. Then he sins again and asks again, and is forgiven again (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). {reward}On the Day of Judgement, the Prophet ﷺ said, Allah will draw a believer close, remind him privately of his sins, and say: I covered them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today{/reward} (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim).

He also tells us what His repeated forgiveness is attached to. He is Ghaffar for whoever repents, believes, does good and then stays on guidance (20:82). The covering is endless, but it is a covering for those who keep turning back, not for those who have stopped caring.
trusting: Some sins are habits. You stop, you fall, you stop again. {trap}The danger is not the fall; it is deciding that asking again is pointless and giving up on Him.{/trap} Al-Ghaffar is the name for the person on their fiftieth attempt. Every sincere return meets a fresh covering.

Hand Him your fear of exposure too. You may dread that what you hide will one day be seen. {idea}The One whose name is Ghaffar loves to conceal{/idea}, and He covered you long before you ever asked. Make your istighfar a daily breath, not an emergency alarm, and let it soften the pressure of the past.
loving: Think of someone who has seen your worst moments and never once brought them up, never told anyone, and greets you each time as if they had forgotten. You would love that person deeply. {reward}Al-Ghaffar has seen everything, covered it from every eye, and still calls you back by name.{/reward}
now: It is Sunday night and you are back at the same screen, the same habit you promised to leave on Friday. The old voice says you are a hypocrite for even asking again. {idea}Al-Ghaffar's answer is to ask anyway{/idea}: close the tab, say astaghfirullah with meaning, and start Monday covered, not condemned.
old: If I keep falling into the same sin, my repeated apologies must be worthless to Allah.
new: Al-Ghaffar forgives again each time I sincerely return, so my next apology is never wasted.
try: Pick a quiet moment today and say astaghfirullah slowly a hundred times, as the Prophet ﷺ used to seek forgiveness many times a day.

dua.text: Ya Ghaffar, You have covered me more times than I can count. Cover me again, forgive what I hide and what I have forgotten, and do not expose me before Your servants.
dua.note: Call on Him as Al-Ghaffar after a repeated slip, when shame tells you not to ask; His name is the promise that asking again is welcome.

pairs.why: Al-Aziz Al-Ghaffar: the One with full power to punish chooses, again and again, to cover and forgive.
Al-Ghaffar stresses how often He forgives; Al-Ghafur stresses how vast His forgiveness is, even for the greatest sins.
Al-Ghaffar covers the sin; Al-Afuww wipes away its very trace.

faq.a: Al-Ghaffar means the Ever-Forgiving or Perpetual Forgiver, the One who covers and forgives sins again and again. It comes from ghafr, to cover and protect, the same root as mighfar, a helmet. The intensive form stresses that His forgiveness is repeated as often as the servant returns.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Ghaffar and Al-Ghafur?
faq.a: Both come from the same root and mean the Forgiving. Scholars commonly explain that Al-Ghaffar emphasises the frequency of His forgiveness, forgiving time after time, while Al-Ghafur emphasises its greatness and depth, forgiving even the gravest sins completely.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Ghaffar and Al-Afuww?
faq.a: Al-Ghaffar covers a sin: it is concealed and its punishment held back. Al-Afuww, from afw, pardons in the sense of wiping a sin away so that no trace remains. Many scholars see afw as the more complete erasure, which is why the Prophet ﷺ taught the dua of Laylat al-Qadr asking for afw.
